meaning: A declaration that something new is beginning, or that understanding has finally dawned.
explanation: God's first spoken command in the creation account. Light comes into being simply because God says so, so the phrase stands for a creative, world-changing beginning.
kjv_text: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.

meaning: Have many children, or more loosely, grow and expand.
explanation: God's blessing on the first humans (and earlier on the sea creatures and birds), repeated to Noah after the flood. It is a blessing of life and abundance, not only a command.
kjv_text: And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.

meaning: The essential thing that gives life or energy to something.
explanation: God formed Adam from the dust and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul. Life itself is presented as a gift breathed in by God.
kjv_text: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

meaning: Something desirable precisely because it is not allowed.
explanation: God told Adam not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. Eve and Adam ate anyway, and that disobedience brought sin and death into the world. The Bible never says the fruit was an apple.
kjv_text: But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.

meaning: A humorous way of referring to woman or a wife.
explanation: God made the first woman from a rib taken from Adam's side and brought her to him. Adam called her "bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh."
kjv_text: And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.

meaning: The complete union of a married couple.
explanation: "Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh." Jesus quoted it when He taught on marriage.
kjv_text: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.

meaning: A flimsy cover for something embarrassing.
explanation: After eating the forbidden fruit, Adam and Eve "knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons."
kjv_text: And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.

saying: By the sweat of your brow
variants: By the sweat of one's brow
meaning: By your own hard, physical work.
explanation: Part of God's word to Adam after the fall: "In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread." Work itself came before the fall, but after it, work became toil.
kjv_text: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.

variants: Ashes to ashes, dust to dust
meaning: Everyone dies and returns to the earth.
explanation: Also from God's words to Adam: "dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return." The fuller "ashes to ashes" wording comes from the Book of Common Prayer burial service, which draws on this verse.
kjv_text: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.

meaning: Asked to dodge responsibility for someone else; "my brother's keeper" now means taking responsibility for others.
explanation: Cain's evasive answer when God asked where Abel was, after Cain had murdered him. The rest of Scripture answers the question with yes: we are responsible for our neighbour.
kjv_text: And the LORD said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother's keeper?

meaning: A sign of disgrace, especially for a terrible crime.
explanation: God "set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him." In Genesis the mark protected Cain, even though he was guilty. Later usage turned it into a brand of shame.
kjv_text: And the LORD said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And the LORD set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.

meaning: Sleep, or a state of drowsiness.
explanation: In Genesis, Nod is the land east of Eden where Cain settled after being sent away. The punning sense of "sleep" came much later, from writers like Jonathan Swift, and plays on nodding off.
kjv_text: And Cain went out from the presence of the LORD, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.

meaning: Exile from a place of innocence or happiness.
explanation: After murdering Abel, Cain "went out from the presence of the LORD, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden." Adam and Eve had been driven out on the east side of the garden too (3:24). John Steinbeck used the phrase as a novel title.
kjv_text: And Cain went out from the presence of the LORD, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.

meaning: Extremely old.
explanation: Methuselah is the longest-lived person recorded in the Bible, at 969 years.
kjv_text: And all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty and nine years: and he died.

meaning: The ordinary human course of life, especially toward failure or death.
explanation: Before the flood, "all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth." Joshua and David used a related phrase, "the way of all the earth", to mean dying. The idiom blends the two senses: human frailty and death.
kjv_text: And God looked upon the earth, and, behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth.

meaning: A place crammed with many kinds of creatures or things; something very old-fashioned.
explanation: God told Noah to build an ark and bring his family and pairs of every kind of animal on board to survive the flood.
kjv_text: Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.

meaning: Make a gesture of peace or reconciliation.
explanation: The dove that Noah sent out came back with a fresh olive leaf, a sign that the floodwaters had gone down and God's judgment was over. That made the olive branch a symbol of peace restored.
kjv_text: And the dove came in to him in the evening; and, lo, in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.

meaning: A confused noise of many voices; a scene of confusion.
explanation: People built a tower to "make us a name", and God confused their language and scattered them. The place was called Babel "because the LORD did there confound the language of all the earth."
kjv_text: Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the LORD did there confound the language of all the earth: and from thence did the LORD scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.

meaning: A place of great wickedness facing judgment.
explanation: "The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous." Abraham pleaded for the cities, but not even ten righteous people were found, and God destroyed them with fire and brimstone.
kjv_text: And the LORD said, Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous;

meaning: Fierce warnings of divine punishment; describes intense, threatening preaching.
explanation: God rained brimstone (sulphur) and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah. Revelation uses the same image for the final judgment.
kjv_text: Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven;

variants: Turned into a pillar of salt
meaning: Frozen in place, especially by looking back or longing for the past.
explanation: Lot's wife looked back at Sodom against the angels' warning and became a pillar of salt. Jesus later warned, "Remember Lot's wife" (Luke 17:32).
kjv_text: But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.

meaning: To die; humorously, for a machine to stop working.
explanation: The KJV's usual phrase for dying: "ghost" is the old English word for spirit. Used of Abraham, and of Jesus on the cross.
kjv_text: Then Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years; and was gathered to his people.

saying: Sell your birthright for a mess of pottage
meaning: Give up something of lasting value for a small, immediate pleasure.
explanation: Esau, hungry from the field, sold his rights as firstborn to Jacob for bread and lentil stew. The phrase "mess of pottage" comes from chapter headings in older English Bibles rather than the KJV text itself. Hebrews 12:16 holds Esau up as a warning.
kjv_text: And Jacob said, Swear to me this day; and he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob. Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright.

meaning: A connection between earth and heaven; also a rope ladder on a ship.
explanation: Fleeing from Esau, Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven with angels going up and down it. God renewed His promise to him there, and Jacob named the place Bethel, "house of God."
kjv_text: And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.

meaning: A bright, multi-coloured garment; a sign of special favour.
explanation: Jacob gave this coat to Joseph, his favourite son. It stirred up his brothers' jealousy and led to Joseph being sold into slavery.
kjv_text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours.

meaning: There's plenty available somewhere, if you go and get it.
explanation: During the famine, Jacob told his sons, "I have heard that there is corn in Egypt: get you down thither, and buy for us." Joseph had stored up grain there.
kjv_text: And he said, Behold, I have heard that there is corn in Egypt: get you down thither, and buy for us from thence; that we may live, and not die.

variants: Live off the fat of the land
meaning: The best and richest things available; living in luxury.
explanation: Pharaoh's promise to Joseph's family: "ye shall eat the fat of the land" of Egypt. "Fat" meant the choicest produce.
kjv_text: And take your father and your households, and come unto me: and I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and ye shall eat the fat of the land.

meaning: A light, portable woven cot for a baby.
explanation: Moses' mother hid him from Pharaoh's decree in "an ark of bulrushes" daubed with pitch among the reeds of the Nile, where Pharaoh's daughter found him.
kjv_text: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river's brink.

saying: A stranger in a strange land
meaning: Someone who feels out of place, far from home.
explanation: Moses, who had fled Egypt to Midian, named his son Gershom, saying, "I have been a stranger in a strange land."
kjv_text: And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.

meaning: A dramatic, unmistakable calling or revelation.
explanation: God appeared to Moses in a bush that burned but was not consumed. From it He called Moses to lead Israel out of Egypt.
kjv_text: And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.

saying: A land flowing with milk and honey
meaning: A place of plenty and prosperity; a promised land.
explanation: God's description of Canaan, the land He promised to bring Israel into after rescuing them from slavery in Egypt.
kjv_text: And I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey; unto the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.

meaning: Deliberately refuse to feel sympathy or change your mind.
explanation: Used of Pharaoh, who again and again refused to let Israel go. Psalm 95 turns it into a warning to God's own people: "Harden not your heart."
kjv_text: And the LORD said unto Moses, When thou goest to return into Egypt, see that thou do all those wonders before Pharaoh, which I have put in thine hand: but I will harden his heart, that he shall not let the people go.

meaning: A demand for freedom from oppression.
explanation: God's message to Pharaoh through Moses and Aaron. It became a rallying cry in African American spirituals and the civil rights movement.
kjv_text: And afterward Moses and Aaron went in, and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.

meaning: Be expected to do a job without the materials needed for it.
explanation: Pharaoh punished the Israelites by making them gather their own straw while still producing the same number of bricks.
kjv_text: Ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves.

meaning: Thick, oppressive darkness.
explanation: The ninth plague on Egypt: "darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt." It lasted three days, yet the Israelites had light where they lived.
kjv_text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt.

variants: Pillar of cloud and pillar of fire
meaning: A guiding sign that leads the way.
explanation: God led Israel through the wilderness "by day in a pillar of a cloud... and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light."
kjv_text: And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night:

meaning: Keep quiet.
explanation: Moses at the Red Sea, with Pharaoh's army closing in: "The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace." The wedding formula "speak now or forever hold your peace" uses the same old phrase.
kjv_text: The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.

meaning: Fail or drop quickly and completely.
explanation: From Moses' song after the Red Sea crossing, describing Pharaoh's army: "they sank into the bottom as a stone."
kjv_text: The depths have covered them: they sank into the bottom as a stone.

meaning: Fail completely, or fall flat.
explanation: From Moses' song at the Red Sea: "the sea covered them: they sank as lead in the mighty waters."
kjv_text: Thou didst blow with thy wind, the sea covered them: they sank as lead in the mighty waters.

meaning: Luxury and indulgence, often remembered with longing.
explanation: The hungry Israelites grumbled in the wilderness: "Would to God we had died... in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots." They missed their full stomachs more than they hated slavery.
kjv_text: And the children of Israel said unto them, Would to God we had died by the hand of the LORD in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots, and when we did eat bread to the full; for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.

meaning: An unexpected blessing or windfall that arrives exactly when needed.
explanation: God fed Israel in the wilderness with bread that appeared each morning. The people called it manna, meaning "What is it?" Jesus later called Himself the true bread from heaven (John 6:32-35).
kjv_text: And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. And Moses said unto them, This is the bread which the LORD hath given you to eat.

meaning: An idol; by extension, anything treated with excessive reverence.
explanation: The second commandment forbids making a carved ("graven") image to worship.
kjv_text: Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:

saying: Take the Lord's name in vain
meaning: Use God's name carelessly; jokingly, talk about someone disrespectfully.
explanation: The third commandment: "for the LORD will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain."
kjv_text: Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain; for the LORD will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.

saying: Honour thy father and thy mother
meaning: Respect and care for your parents.
explanation: The fifth commandment, which Paul calls "the first commandment with promise": "that thy days may be long upon the land."
kjv_text: Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.

meaning: Tell lies about someone.
explanation: The ninth commandment: "Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour."
kjv_text: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.

variants: An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth
meaning: Punishment should match the offence; often used to mean revenge.
explanation: In the Law this set a limit on justice in the courts, so the penalty could be no greater than the harm done. It was never a licence for personal revenge. Jesus quoted it and called His followers beyond it: "resist not evil" and turn the other cheek.
kjv_text: Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,

meaning: Fixed and unchangeable.
explanation: God gave Moses the law on two tablets of stone, "written with the finger of God", a picture of permanent, authoritative words.
kjv_text: And he gave unto Moses, when he had made an end of communing with him upon mount Sinai, two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God.

meaning: Something, especially wealth, that people wrongly idolise.
explanation: While Moses was on Mount Sinai, Aaron made a gold calf from the people's earrings, and Israel worshipped it. It was a notorious act of idolatry.
kjv_text: And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

meaning: Stubborn and proud.
explanation: God's description of Israel after the golden calf. The picture is of an ox that won't bend its neck to the yoke.
kjv_text: And the LORD said unto Moses, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people:

meaning: A gift given to make up after a quarrel.
explanation: In the Law, the peace offering was a sacrifice celebrating fellowship between God and the worshipper, and part of it was eaten as a shared meal.
kjv_text: And if his oblation be a sacrifice of peace offering, if he offer it of the herd; whether it be a male or female, he shall offer it without blemish before the LORD.

meaning: Someone made to take the blame for others.
explanation: On the Day of Atonement, the high priest confessed Israel's sins over a live goat and sent it into the wilderness, carrying their sins away. The word "scapegoat" was coined by William Tyndale for this passage.
kjv_text: But the goat, on which the lot fell to be the scapegoat, shall be presented alive before the LORD, to make an atonement with him, and to let him go for a scapegoat into the wilderness.

meaning: Treat others with the same care you want for yourself.
explanation: A command from the Law that Jesus named the second greatest, alongside loving God. The parable of the Good Samaritan shows that anyone in need is our neighbour.
kjv_text: Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the LORD.

meaning: A special anniversary celebration.
explanation: Every fiftieth year Israel was to "proclaim liberty throughout all the land": slaves were freed, debts forgiven and land returned to its families. The KJV spells it "jubile".
kjv_text: And ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubile unto you; and ye shall return every man unto his possession, and ye shall return every man unto his family.

meaning: Investigate a situation before acting.
explanation: Moses sent twelve men to "spy out the land of Canaan". Ten came back afraid, and only Joshua and Caleb trusted God to give it.
kjv_text: And Moses sent them to spy out the land of Canaan, and said unto them, Get you up this way southward, and go up into the mountain:

saying: Be sure your sin will find you out
variants: Your sins will find you out
meaning: Wrongdoing will eventually be discovered.
explanation: Moses warned the tribes of Reuben and Gad that if they broke their promise to fight alongside their brothers, they would be sinning against the LORD: "be sure your sin will find you out."
kjv_text: But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the LORD: and be sure your sin will find you out.

meaning: Choose what leads to life and flourishing.
explanation: Moses' final challenge to Israel: "I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live."
kjv_text: I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:

meaning: Someone deeply loved and protected.
explanation: "Apple" meant the pupil, the part of the eye a person instinctively guards. God kept Israel "as the apple of his eye", and David prayed to be kept the same way.
kjv_text: He found him in a desert land, and in the waste howling wilderness; he led him about, he instructed him, he kept him as the apple of his eye.

meaning: Forces of nature or destiny, beyond human control.
explanation: Deborah's song of victory over Sisera: "The stars in their courses fought against Sisera." Even the heavens were on Israel's side.
kjv_text: They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera.

meaning: A word, custom or belief that marks someone as an insider or outsider.
explanation: The Gileadites caught fleeing Ephraimites by asking them to say "Shibboleth". The Ephraimites couldn't pronounce it and said "Sibboleth", which gave them away.
kjv_text: Then said they unto him, Say now Shibboleth: and he said Sibboleth: for he could not frame to pronounce it right. Then they took him, and slew him at the passages of Jordan: and there fell at that time of the Ephraimites forty and two thousand.

saying: Out of the strong came forth sweetness
meaning: Good can come out of something harsh.
explanation: Samson's riddle, based on the honey he found in the carcass of a lion he had killed.
kjv_text: And he said unto them, Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness. And they could not in three days expound the riddle.

meaning: Defeat someone completely.
explanation: Samson's revenge on the Philistines: "he smote them hip and thigh with a great slaughter."
kjv_text: And he smote them hip and thigh with a great slaughter: and he went down and dwelt in the top of the rock Etam.

meaning: A seductive, treacherous woman.
explanation: Delilah was paid by the Philistine lords to find the secret of Samson's strength. She betrayed him to his enemies.
kjv_text: And it came to pass afterward, that he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah. And the lords of the Philistines came up unto her, and said unto her, Entice him, and see wherein his great strength lieth, and by what means we may prevail against him, that we may bind him to afflict him: and we will give thee every one of us eleven hundred pieces of silver.

meaning: All together, in complete unity.
explanation: "All the people arose as one man." The tribes of Israel gathered as one to respond to the outrage at Gibeah.
kjv_text: And all the people arose as one man, saying, We will not any of us go to his tent, neither will we any of us turn into his house.

saying: Doing what is right in your own eyes
variants: Every man did what was right in his own eyes
meaning: Everyone following their own rules.
explanation: The closing line of Judges: "In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes." It sums up the chaos of the period.
kjv_text: In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.

saying: Whither thou goest, I will go
variants: Your people will be my people
meaning: A pledge of complete loyalty, often used in weddings.
explanation: Ruth to her widowed mother-in-law Naomi: "thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God."
kjv_text: And Ruth said, Intreat me not to leave thee, or to return from following after thee: for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God:

meaning: A loyal greeting to a monarch.
explanation: The people's shout when Samuel presented Saul as Israel's first king. It is repeated for later kings too (2 Samuel 16:16; 1 Kings 1:39).
kjv_text: And Samuel said to all the people, See ye him whom the LORD hath chosen, that there is none like him among all the people? And all the people shouted, and said, God save the king.

saying: A man after my own heart
variants: A man after his own heart
meaning: Someone who shares your tastes and values.
explanation: Samuel told Saul that God had found "a man after his own heart" to replace him. That man was David, chosen for his devotion to God rather than his outward appearance.
kjv_text: But now thy kingdom shall not continue: the LORD hath sought him a man after his own heart, and the LORD hath commanded him to be captain over his people, because thou hast not kept that which the LORD commanded thee.

saying: To obey is better than sacrifice
meaning: Doing what is right matters more than outward displays of devotion.
explanation: Samuel's rebuke to Saul, who kept plunder he had been told to destroy and claimed it was for sacrifices.
kjv_text: And Samuel said, Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.

meaning: A contest where the weak underdog faces, and may beat, a much stronger opponent.
explanation: The shepherd boy David defeated the Philistine giant Goliath with a sling and a stone. He trusted that "the battle is the LORD's" (1 Samuel 17:47).
kjv_text: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and smote the Philistine, and slew him; but there was no sword in the hand of David.

meaning: A deep, loyal friendship.
explanation: Jonathan, King Saul's son, loved David "as his own soul". He protected David from his own father even though it cost him the throne.
kjv_text: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.

meaning: Behave foolishly.
explanation: Saul, after David spared his life a second time: "Behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly."
kjv_text: Then said Saul, I have sinned: return, my son David: for I will no more do thee harm, because my soul was precious in thine eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.

meaning: Take the blame, often by resigning.
explanation: Badly wounded at Mount Gilboa, King Saul "took a sword, and fell upon it" rather than be captured by the Philistines.
kjv_text: Then said Saul unto his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me. But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid. Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell upon it.

meaning: Said, often with satisfaction, when someone powerful suffers a downfall.
explanation: From David's lament over Saul and Jonathan: "how are the mighty fallen!" In the Bible it is sincere grief, not gloating.
kjv_text: The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places: how are the mighty fallen!

meaning: Keep this embarrassing news from our rivals.
explanation: David's lament for Saul and Jonathan: "publish it not in the streets of Askelon; lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice."
kjv_text: Tell it not in Gath, publish it not in the streets of Askelon; lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.

meaning: A friendship deeper than romantic love.
explanation: David mourning Jonathan: "very pleasant hast thou been unto me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women."
kjv_text: I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant hast thou been unto me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.

meaning: Someone's single most precious possession.
explanation: Nathan's parable to David: a rich man took a poor man's only lamb. David was outraged, and Nathan told him, "Thou art the man."
kjv_text: But the poor man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished up: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own meat, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was unto him as a daughter.

meaning: Claim someone said something they did not say, or tell them what to say.
explanation: Joab coached a wise woman from Tekoa with a story to tell King David, to persuade him to bring Absalom home: "So Joab put the words in her mouth."
kjv_text: And come to the king, and speak on this manner unto him. So Joab put the words in her mouth.

meaning: I wouldn't presume to (usually said before doing just that).
explanation: Joab, besieging a city, denied he wanted to destroy it: "Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy."
kjv_text: And Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy.

meaning: A wise decision that reveals the truth or fairly settles a dispute.
explanation: Two women claimed the same baby. Solomon ordered it cut in two, and the real mother gave up her claim to save the child, which showed who she was.
kjv_text: And the king said, Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other.

meaning: Exceptional wisdom and good judgment.
explanation: God gave King Solomon wisdom beyond anyone of his time. He showed it most famously in the case of two women who both claimed the same baby.
kjv_text: And Solomon's wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt.

variants: Who do you think you are, the Queen of Sheba?
meaning: Someone acting grand or self-important.
explanation: The wealthy queen travelled to test Solomon with hard questions and brought gold, spices and precious stones.
kjv_text: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to prove him with hard questions.

saying: The half was not told me
meaning: Reality is even better than what you heard.
explanation: The Queen of Sheba, after seeing Solomon's wisdom and wealth for herself.
kjv_text: Howbeit I believed not the words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it: and, behold, the half was not told me: thy wisdom and prosperity exceedeth the fame which I heard.

meaning: Treat people even more harshly than before.
explanation: Rehoboam's foolish reply to Israel's request for lighter burdens: "my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions." Ten tribes broke away.
kjv_text: And now whereas my father did lade you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke: my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.

variants: A cruse of oil that never fails
meaning: A small supply that never runs out.
explanation: During the famine, the widow of Zarephath shared her last meal with Elijah. Her barrel of meal and cruse (jar) of oil never ran out.
kjv_text: And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by Elijah.

saying: A cloud no bigger than a man's hand
meaning: A tiny early sign of something big to come.
explanation: After three years of drought, Elijah's servant saw "a little cloud out of the sea, like a man's hand." Soon the sky was black with a great rain.
kjv_text: And it came to pass at the seventh time, that he said, Behold, there ariseth a little cloud out of the sea, like a man's hand. And he said, Go up, say unto Ahab, Prepare thy chariot, and get thee down, that the rain stop thee not.

meaning: Get ready for something difficult.
explanation: People in the ancient world tucked their long robes into a belt so they could run or work. Elijah girded up his loins and ran ahead of Ahab's chariot.
kjv_text: And the hand of the LORD was on Elijah; and he girded up his loins, and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.

meaning: The quiet inner voice of conscience or of God.
explanation: On Mount Horeb, God was not in the wind, the earthquake or the fire. He spoke to the exhausted Elijah in "a still small voice."
kjv_text: And after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.

meaning: A shameless, scheming or immoral woman.
explanation: Queen Jezebel, wife of King Ahab, promoted Baal worship, persecuted God's prophets and arranged Naboth's murder to seize his vineyard.
kjv_text: But there was none like unto Ahab, which did sell himself to work wickedness in the sight of the LORD, whom Jezebel his wife stirred up.

saying: Draw a bow at a venture
meaning: Make a random guess or attempt that happens to hit its mark.
explanation: A soldier shot an arrow at random and struck the disguised King Ahab between the joints of his armour, fulfilling Micaiah's prophecy.
kjv_text: And a certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Israel between the joints of the harness: wherefore he said unto the driver of his chariot, Turn thine hand, and carry me out of the host; for I am wounded.

meaning: A glorious, heavenly departure or unseen spiritual strength.
explanation: Elijah was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind as a chariot and horses of fire parted him from Elisha. Later, God opened a servant's eyes to see hills full of chariots of fire protecting Elisha.
kjv_text: And it came to pass, as they still went on, and talked, that, behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

meaning: Drive recklessly fast.
explanation: The watchman recognised Jehu's chariot from far away: "the driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi; for he driveth furiously."
kjv_text: And the watchman told, saying, He came even unto them, and cometh not again: and the driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi; for he driveth furiously.

meaning: Sort out your affairs, often before a major change or death.
explanation: Isaiah's message to the sick King Hezekiah: "Set thine house in order; for thou shalt die." Hezekiah prayed, and God added fifteen years to his life.
kjv_text: In those days was Hezekiah sick unto death. And the prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz came to him, and said unto him, Thus saith the LORD, Set thine house in order; for thou shalt die, and not live.

saying: For such a time as this
meaning: A person seems placed in a situation for a special purpose.
explanation: Mordecai urged Queen Esther to risk her life to save her people: "who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?"
kjv_text: For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place; but thou and thy father's house shall be destroyed: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?

saying: The Lord gives and the Lord takes away
variants: The Lord giveth and the Lord taketh away
meaning: An acceptance that both blessing and loss are in God's hands.
explanation: Job's response after losing his children and wealth in a single day. It ends: "blessed be the name of the LORD."
kjv_text: And said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.

meaning: Hardship is part of human life.
explanation: Eliphaz to Job: "Yet man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward."
kjv_text: Yet man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward.

meaning: Very old or long familiar.
explanation: Eliphaz mocks Job: "Art thou the first man that was born? or wast thou made before the hills?" The hills stand for the oldest things on earth.
kjv_text: Art thou the first man that was born? or wast thou made before the hills?

meaning: Someone who makes you feel worse while claiming to comfort you.
explanation: Job's three friends insisted his suffering must be punishment for secret sin. Job called them "miserable comforters", and God later rebuked them (Job 42:7).
kjv_text: I have heard many such things: miserable comforters are ye all.

saying: By the skin of your teeth
meaning: Only just; by the narrowest margin.
explanation: Job, wasted by suffering, says, "I am escaped with the skin of my teeth." Teeth have no skin, so he means he has barely survived with nothing left.
kjv_text: My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, and I am escaped with the skin of my teeth.

meaning: The central, underlying cause of something.
explanation: Job warns his friends who keep insisting "the root of the matter is found in me", that is, that the cause of his trouble lies in his own sin.
kjv_text: But ye should say, Why persecute we him, seeing the root of the matter is found in me?

meaning: Something enormous and powerful.
explanation: God points Job to the behemoth, a massive beast "which I made with thee", to show His power over creation.
kjv_text: Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox.

meaning: Something huge and formidable.
explanation: "Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook?" God describes a fearsome sea creature that no human can tame.
kjv_text: Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord which thou lettest down?

saying: Out of the mouths of babes
variants: Out of the mouths of babes and sucklings
meaning: Children often say wise or telling things without realising it.
explanation: God ordains praise "out of the mouth of babes and sucklings." Jesus quoted it when children cried "Hosanna" in the temple and the chief priests objected.
kjv_text: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou ordained strength because of thine enemies, that thou mightest still the enemy and the avenger.

meaning: What someone wants most of all.
explanation: David thanks God: "Thou hast given him his heart's desire." Psalm 37:4 links it to delighting in the Lord.
kjv_text: Thou hast given him his heart's desire, and hast not withholden the request of his lips. Selah.

meaning: Mock someone openly.
explanation: "All they that see me laugh me to scorn." David's psalm is echoed at the crucifixion. At Jairus's house, the mourners "laughed him to scorn" too.
kjv_text: All they that see me laugh me to scorn: they shoot out the lip, they shake the head saying,

meaning: Trust that God will guide and provide.
explanation: The opening of David's best-loved psalm: "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want."
kjv_text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.

saying: The valley of the shadow of death
meaning: A time of great danger, grief or darkness.
explanation: From the Shepherd Psalm: "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me."
kjv_text: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.

meaning: I have more blessings than I need.
explanation: David pictures God as a generous host who anoints his head with oil and fills his cup to overflowing, even in front of his enemies.
kjv_text: Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.

meaning: Kind care; now often used ironically for harsh treatment ("left to their tender mercies").
explanation: A frequent phrase in Psalms for God's compassion: "Remember, O LORD, thy tender mercies and thy lovingkindnesses."
kjv_text: Remember, O LORD, thy tender mercies and thy lovingkindnesses; for they have been ever of old.

meaning: Being alive, or being back to normal life after illness.
explanation: David says he would have fainted "unless I had believed to see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living."
kjv_text: I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.

meaning: Deep emotional pain, especially from love or loss.
explanation: "The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart." In the Psalms a broken heart is also humble, and God draws near to it and heals it.
kjv_text: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.

saying: Flourish like a green bay tree
meaning: Prosper greatly, often undeservedly.
explanation: "I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a green bay tree. Yet he passed away."
kjv_text: I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a green bay tree.

meaning: Something profound speaks to something equally profound in another.
explanation: The psalmist, downcast and far from the temple, hears roaring waterfalls: "all thy waves and thy billows are gone over me."
kjv_text: Deep calleth unto deep at the noise of thy waterspouts: all thy waves and thy billows are gone over me.

saying: Be still, and know that I am God
meaning: Stop striving and trust God's control.
explanation: In the middle of war and upheaval, God tells the nations to stop fighting and recognise that He is God, "I will be exalted among the nations."
kjv_text: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.

meaning: Utterly pure or clean.
explanation: David's prayer of repentance after his sin with Bathsheba: "wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow."
kjv_text: Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

meaning: Share your deepest feelings openly.
explanation: "Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us."
kjv_text: Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. Selah.

meaning: Die, fail or be defeated.
explanation: "His enemies shall lick the dust." To fall face-down before a conqueror was a sign of total defeat. The modern wording was popularised later, but lists of biblical idioms often trace it to this verse.
kjv_text: They that dwell in the wilderness shall bow before him; and his enemies shall lick the dust.

meaning: Getting steadily more successful.
explanation: Pilgrims on the way to Zion "go from strength to strength." God renews their strength along the journey.
kjv_text: They go from strength to strength, every one of them in Zion appeareth before God.

meaning: A normal human lifespan of seventy years.
explanation: Moses' psalm reflects on how short life is: "The days of our years are threescore years and ten." A score is twenty.
kjv_text: The days of our years are threescore years and ten; and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years, yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.

meaning: Protect and guide someone less experienced.
explanation: "He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust." Jesus used the same image of a hen gathering her chicks.
kjv_text: He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.

saying: As far as the east is from the west
meaning: Completely and immeasurably far apart.
explanation: "As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us." It describes how completely God forgives.
kjv_text: As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us.

meaning: Very close to dying.
explanation: The psalm describes the sick who "draw near unto the gates of death". They cry to the Lord, and He heals them.
kjv_text: Their soul abhorreth all manner of meat; and they draw near unto the gates of death.

meaning: So worried or stressed that you don't know what to do.
explanation: Sailors in a storm "reel to and fro... and are at their wit's end." Then they cry to the Lord, and He calms the sea.
kjv_text: They reel to and fro, and stagger like a drunken man, and are at their wit's end.

saying: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom
meaning: Wisdom starts with reverence for God.
explanation: A theme running through the wisdom books. The "fear" meant is awe and reverence, not terror.
kjv_text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever. Psalm 112

meaning: Nobody can be fully trusted.
explanation: "I said in my haste, All men are liars." The psalmist admits he spoke rashly in his distress.
kjv_text: I said in my haste, All men are liars.

meaning: Someone dismissed by others who turns out to be the most important.
explanation: "The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner." Jesus applied it to Himself, and Paul calls Christ the "chief corner stone."
kjv_text: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.

meaning: Extremely pleasant.
explanation: "How sweet are thy words unto my taste! yea, sweeter than honey to my mouth!"
kjv_text: How sweet are thy words unto my taste! yea, sweeter than honey to my mouth!

meaning: Work hard for nothing.
explanation: "Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it."
kjv_text: Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.

meaning: From a place of deep despair.
explanation: "Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O LORD." The psalm moves from despair to hope in God's forgiveness. Its Latin title, De profundis, became an idiom of its own.
kjv_text: Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O LORD.

meaning: Grief and longing in exile.
explanation: The exiles in Babylon "sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion."
kjv_text: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion.

meaning: Every person is an amazing creation.
explanation: David praises God for forming him in the womb: "I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made."
kjv_text: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.

saying: Put not your trust in princes
meaning: Don't rely on powerful people.
explanation: "...nor in the son of man, in whom there is no help." Human leaders die, but God keeps faith for ever.
kjv_text: Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man, in whom there is no help.

meaning: Of the highest value.
explanation: Said of wisdom, and in Proverbs 31 of a virtuous wife, whose "price is far above rubies."
kjv_text: She is more precious than rubies: and all the things thou canst desire are not to be compared unto her.

saying: Go to the ant, thou sluggard
meaning: Lazy people should learn from the hardworking ant.
explanation: "...consider her ways, and be wise." The ant gathers food in summer with no one making it do so.
kjv_text: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:

saying: Hope deferred makes the heart sick
meaning: Waiting a long time for something hoped for wears a person down.
explanation: "Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life."
kjv_text: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.

saying: Spare the rod and spoil the child
meaning: Children who are never corrected grow up badly.
explanation: "He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes." The proverb is about loving correction. The rhyming modern wording comes from Samuel Butler's 17th-century poem Hudibras.
kjv_text: He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.

saying: A soft answer turneth away wrath
variants: A gentle answer turns away wrath
meaning: A calm, gentle reply cools an angry situation.
explanation: "A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger."
kjv_text: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

meaning: Arrogance leads to downfall.
explanation: "Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall." The saying merges the verse's two halves.
kjv_text: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.

saying: The hoary head is a crown of glory
variants: Grey hair is a crown of glory
meaning: Old age deserves honour.
explanation: "...if it be found in the way of righteousness." "Hoary" means grey or white with age.
kjv_text: The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness.

saying: A friend that sticketh closer than a brother
variants: A friend closer than a brother
meaning: A friend more loyal than family.
explanation: "A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother."
kjv_text: A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.

saying: A good name is better than riches
meaning: Reputation is worth more than wealth.
explanation: "A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold."
kjv_text: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.

saying: Train up a child in the way he should go
meaning: What children are taught stays with them for life.
explanation: "...and when he is old, he will not depart from it."
kjv_text: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.

saying: The borrower is servant to the lender
meaning: Being in debt means losing your freedom.
explanation: "The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender."
kjv_text: The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.

meaning: Wealth can vanish suddenly.
explanation: "For riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven."
kjv_text: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? for riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven.

variants: As a man thinketh in his heart, so is he
meaning: Your thoughts shape who you are.
explanation: In context it warns about a stingy host whose words say "Eat and drink" while his heart is not with you. The line was made famous by James Allen's 1903 book As a Man Thinketh.
kjv_text: For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; but his heart is not with thee.

meaning: Deep sadness.
explanation: "As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather... so is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart." Cheerful songs at the wrong time only add to grief.
kjv_text: As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.

meaning: Out of place and unfitting.
explanation: "As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly for a fool."
kjv_text: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly for a fool.

saying: A dog returns to its vomit
variants: Like a dog returning to its vomit
meaning: Fools repeat the same mistakes.
explanation: "As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly." Peter applies it to those who go back to the sins they escaped.
kjv_text: As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly.

saying: He who digs a pit will fall into it
meaning: Schemes against others backfire on the schemer.
explanation: "Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him."
kjv_text: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.

meaning: People improve each other through honest challenge and friendship.
explanation: "Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend."
kjv_text: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.

saying: The wicked flee when no man pursueth
meaning: A guilty conscience makes people jumpy and afraid.
explanation: "The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion."
kjv_text: The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.

saying: Where there is no vision, the people perish
meaning: Without a clear sense of direction, a group falls apart.
explanation: "Vision" here means prophetic revelation from God. Without it, people "cast off restraint". Today the line is widely quoted in leadership circles.
kjv_text: Where there is no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy is he.

meaning: Everything is ultimately empty and pointless.
explanation: The Preacher's refrain. "Vanity" means a breath or vapour, something fleeting. Ecclesiastes concludes that meaning is found in fearing God (12:13).
kjv_text: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.

variants: There is nothing new under the sun
meaning: Everything has happened before.
explanation: "The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be... and there is no new thing under the sun." Life "under the sun", seen without God, goes round in cycles.
kjv_text: The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.

saying: To everything there is a season
meaning: Every activity or event has its proper time.
explanation: It opens the famous poem on time: a time to be born and a time to die, a time to weep and a time to laugh.
kjv_text: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:

meaning: Partnership is stronger than going it alone.
explanation: "...because they have a good reward for their labour. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow." Verse 12 adds, "a threefold cord is not quickly broken."
kjv_text: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.

meaning: Enjoy life while you can.
explanation: The Preacher commends simple enjoyment as God's gift. Jesus' parable of the rich fool shows its dark side: the man said "eat, drink, and be merry" and died that night, "not rich toward God."
kjv_text: Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide with him of his labour the days of his life, which God giveth him under the sun.

saying: A living dog is better than a dead lion
meaning: Being alive, however lowly, beats glorious death; while there's life there's hope.
explanation: "For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope." Dogs were despised and lions admired.
kjv_text: For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.

saying: The race is not to the swift
meaning: Success does not always go to the most talented; chance plays a part.
explanation: "The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong... but time and chance happeneth to them all."
kjv_text: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.

meaning: A small flaw that spoils something good.
explanation: "Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom."
kjv_text: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honour.

variants: Money is the answer to everything
meaning: Money solves every problem, usually said cynically.
explanation: The Preacher's observation about feasting and wine: "a feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all things."
kjv_text: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all things.

meaning: I heard it from a source I won't name.
explanation: "Curse not the king, no not in thy thought... for a bird of the air shall carry the voice." Private words have a way of getting out.
kjv_text: Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.

saying: Cast your bread upon the waters
meaning: Give or invest generously without expecting an immediate return.
explanation: "Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days." Generosity will bear fruit in time.
kjv_text: Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.

saying: Of making many books there is no end
meaning: There is always more being written; endless study is exhausting.
explanation: "Of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh."
kjv_text: And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.

meaning: Everything that is required of a person.
explanation: The Preacher's conclusion: "Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man."
kjv_text: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.

meaning: An image of beauty and purity; the names of flowers.
explanation: The beloved says, "I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys." Christian hymns later applied both titles to Christ.
kjv_text: I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys.

meaning: Someone good and beautiful in a harsh setting.
explanation: "As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters."
kjv_text: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.

saying: The little foxes that spoil the vines
meaning: Small, overlooked problems that do great damage.
explanation: "Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes."
kjv_text: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.

meaning: Love is unbreakable.
explanation: "Set me as a seal upon thine heart... for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave."
kjv_text: Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave: the coals thereof are coals of fire, which hath a most vehement flame.

meaning: True love cannot be put out.
explanation: "...neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned."
kjv_text: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.

meaning: Completely pure or clean.
explanation: "Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow." God's offer of cleansing and forgiveness.
kjv_text: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

meaning: Turn from war to peaceful work.
explanation: The prophets' picture of the age of peace when God judges the nations: "they shall beat their swords into plowshares... neither shall they learn war any more."
kjv_text: And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

saying: Grind the faces of the poor
meaning: Oppress people who are already struggling.
explanation: God's charge against Judah's leaders: "What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor?"
kjv_text: What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor? saith the LORD GOD of hosts.

saying: Call evil good and good evil
meaning: Turn moral values upside down.
explanation: "Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness."
kjv_text: Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!

meaning: An expression of distress, now often jokingly self-pitying.
explanation: Isaiah's cry when he saw the holy Lord in the temple: "Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips." Then a seraph touched his lips with a coal and took away his sin.
kjv_text: Then said I, Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts.

meaning: A title for Christ; someone who brings peace.
explanation: One of the names of the promised child: "Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace."
kjv_text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.

saying: The lion shall lie down with the lamb
meaning: Sworn enemies living together in peace.
explanation: Isaiah's picture of the Messiah's kingdom: "The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid." The popular lion-and-lamb wording blends these lines.
kjv_text: The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.

saying: The four corners of the earth
meaning: Everywhere in the world.
explanation: God will gather His scattered people "from the four corners of the earth." It is a picture of the whole earth, from every direction.
kjv_text: And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

meaning: Support in words only, not in action.
explanation: "This people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me." Jesus quoted it against the Pharisees.
kjv_text: Wherefore the Lord said, Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men:

meaning: Someone or something too weak to rely on.
explanation: The Assyrian commander mocked Judah for trusting Egypt, "this broken reed, on which if a man lean, it will go into his hand, and pierce it."
kjv_text: Lo, thou trustest in the staff of this broken reed, on Egypt; whereon if a man lean, it will go into his hand, and pierce it: so is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all that trust in him.

saying: In the hollow of his hand
meaning: Completely under someone's control or protection.
explanation: "Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and meted out heaven with the span?"
kjv_text: Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and meted out heaven with the span, and comprehended the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?

meaning: An amount far too small to matter.
explanation: "Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket" beside the greatness of God.
kjv_text: Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket, and are counted as the small dust of the balance: behold, he taketh up the isles as a very little thing.

saying: Mount up with wings as eagles
meaning: Rise above difficulty with renewed strength.
explanation: "They that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary."
kjv_text: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.

meaning: Someone fragile who needs gentle treatment.
explanation: Of God's Servant: "A bruised reed shall he not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench." Matthew applies it to Jesus.
kjv_text: A bruised reed shall he not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench: he shall bring forth judgment unto truth.

variants: To the ends of the earth
meaning: The most distant places imaginable.
explanation: "Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth." Jesus sent His witnesses "unto the uttermost part of the earth."
kjv_text: Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth: for I am God, and there is none else.

meaning: Said humorously when you have too much to do.
explanation: "There is no peace, saith the LORD, unto the wicked." Isaiah 57:20 compares the wicked to "the troubled sea, when it cannot rest."
kjv_text: There is no peace, saith the LORD, unto the wicked.

meaning: Timely, well-chosen advice.
explanation: "The Lord GOD hath given me the tongue of the learned, that I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary."
kjv_text: The Lord GOD hath given me the tongue of the learned, that I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary: he wakeneth morning by morning, he wakeneth mine ear to hear as the learned.

saying: Set your face like a flint
meaning: Be utterly determined.
explanation: The Servant, facing abuse: "therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed." Luke 9:51 echoes it as Jesus sets out for Jerusalem.
kjv_text: For the Lord GOD will help me; therefore shall I not be confounded: therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed.

meaning: Agree completely.
explanation: "They shall see eye to eye, when the LORD shall bring again Zion." The watchmen see God's return face to face. The modern sense of agreeing grew out of it.
kjv_text: Thy watchmen shall lift up the voice; with the voice together shall they sing: for they shall see eye to eye, when the LORD shall bring again Zion.

meaning: Someone who has known great grief.
explanation: The Suffering Servant is "despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief." Christians see Jesus in this prophecy.
kjv_text: He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.

saying: Like a lamb to the slaughter
meaning: Going unaware or without resistance to a terrible fate.
explanation: The Suffering Servant "is brought as a lamb to the slaughter" and stays silent. The New Testament applies this to Jesus.
kjv_text: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth.

meaning: Wake up and get going.
explanation: "Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee." Originally a call to Zion to reflect God's glory.
kjv_text: Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee.

meaning: Something good brought out of grief or loss.
explanation: The Messiah comes "to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning." Jesus read from this passage in Nazareth (Luke 4:18-21).
kjv_text: To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.

meaning: Smugly self-righteous.
explanation: God condemns people who say, "Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou." Their pride is "a smoke in my nose."
kjv_text: Which say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou. These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burneth all the day.

saying: Is there no balm in Gilead?
meaning: Is there no remedy or comfort to be found?
explanation: Jeremiah grieving over his people: "is there no physician there? why then is not the health of the daughter of my people recovered?" Gilead was famous for healing balm.
kjv_text: Is there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there? why then is not the health of the daughter of my people recovered?

saying: Can a leopard change its spots?
variants: A leopard can't change its spots
meaning: People cannot change their basic nature.
explanation: "Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? then may ye also do good, that are accustomed to do evil." Only God can change a heart (Jeremiah 31:33).
kjv_text: Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? then may ye also do good, that are accustomed to do evil.

saying: Like clay in the potter's hands
meaning: Completely shaped by someone else's will.
explanation: At the potter's house God tells Jeremiah: "as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Israel."
kjv_text: O house of Israel, cannot I do with you as this potter? saith the LORD. Behold, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Israel.

meaning: Irritate or annoy intensely.
explanation: A proverb: "The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the children's teeth are set on edge." God rejects it: each person will answer for their own sin (31:30; Ezekiel 18:2-4).
kjv_text: In those days they shall say no more, The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the children's teeth are set on edge.

meaning: A situation with hidden, complicated workings.
explanation: In Ezekiel's vision of the living creatures, their wheels looked like "a wheel in the middle of a wheel."
kjv_text: The appearance of the wheels and their work was like unto the colour of a beryl: and they four had one likeness: and their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel.

meaning: Daughters take after their mothers.
explanation: "Behold, every one that useth proverbs shall use this proverb against thee, saying, As is the mother, so is her daughter."
kjv_text: Behold, every one that useth proverbs shall use this proverb against thee, saying, As is the mother, so is her daughter.

meaning: The point where a decision must be made or people go separate ways.
explanation: "The king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way", using divination to choose whether to attack Jerusalem or Ammon.
kjv_text: For the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination: he made his arrows bright, he consulted with images, he looked in the liver.

meaning: Abundant good things.
explanation: God's promise to restore His flock: "I will cause the shower to come down in his season; there shall be showers of blessing."
kjv_text: And I will make them and the places round about my hill a blessing; and I will cause the shower to come down in his season; there shall be showers of blessing.

meaning: Being cold and unfeeling.
explanation: God promises, "I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh."
kjv_text: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.

meaning: Something lifeless that needs reviving.
explanation: In a vision, Ezekiel prophesied to a valley of dry bones. They came together and lived, a picture of God restoring Israel.
kjv_text: Again he said unto me, Prophesy upon these bones, and say unto them, O ye dry bones, hear the word of the LORD.

meaning: A hidden weakness in someone greatly admired.
explanation: Nebuchadnezzar dreamed of a great statue made of gold, silver, bronze and iron, standing on feet of iron mixed with clay. A stone struck the weak feet and the whole statue fell.
kjv_text: His legs of iron, his feet part of iron and part of clay.

meaning: An ordeal of extreme heat or testing.
explanation: Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego were thrown in for refusing to worship Nebuchadnezzar's image. A fourth figure walked with them in the fire, and they came out unharmed.
kjv_text: And whoso falleth not down and worshippeth shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.

meaning: A clear sign that disaster is coming.
explanation: At Belshazzar's feast a hand wrote on the palace wall. Daniel read it as God's judgment: the kingdom was finished, and Babylon fell that night.
kjv_text: In the same hour came forth fingers of a man's hand, and wrote over against the candlestick upon the plaister of the wall of the king's palace: and the king saw the part of the hand that wrote.

saying: Weighed in the balance and found wanting
meaning: Judged and found not good enough.
explanation: Daniel's reading of the writing on the wall for King Belshazzar: "TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting." The king died that very night.
kjv_text: TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting.

saying: The law of the Medes and Persians
meaning: A rule that can never be changed.
explanation: Daniel's enemies tricked King Darius into signing a decree that, under Persian law, "altereth not", so Daniel was thrown to the lions.
kjv_text: Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it be not changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not.

meaning: Into a hostile, dangerous situation.
explanation: Daniel was thrown into a den of lions for praying to God. God shut the lions' mouths, and Daniel came out unharmed.
kjv_text: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions. Now the king spake and said unto Daniel, Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee.

saying: Sow the wind and reap the whirlwind
meaning: Suffer severe consequences for foolish actions.
explanation: "They have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind." Israel's idolatry would bring disaster far greater than its seed.
kjv_text: For they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind: it hath no stalk: the bud shall yield no meal: if so be it yield, the strangers shall swallow it up.

saying: The years that the locust hath eaten
meaning: Wasted or lost years.
explanation: God's promise after judgment: "I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten."
kjv_text: And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpiller, and the palmerworm, my great army which I sent among you.

saying: Can two walk together unless they agree?
meaning: Partners must share a common purpose.
explanation: One of a series of rhetorical questions from Amos, showing that every effect has a cause, and so does God's warning.
kjv_text: Can two walk together, except they be agreed?

saying: Let justice roll down like waters
meaning: A call for justice to flow freely and without end.
explanation: "But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream." Martin Luther King Jr. famously quoted it.
kjv_text: But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.

meaning: Someone who brings bad luck.
explanation: Sailors in a storm cast lots to find who was to blame, and the lot fell on Jonah, who was running from God. They threw him overboard and the sea grew calm.
kjv_text: And they said every one to his fellow, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.

saying: Do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly
meaning: A summary of a good life.
explanation: "He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?"
kjv_text: He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?

variants: Put wages into a bag with holes
meaning: Money that vanishes as fast as it comes.
explanation: God told the returned exiles that while they neglected His house, "he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes."
kjv_text: Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes.

meaning: A hard trial that purifies.
explanation: Of the coming messenger of the covenant: "who shall stand when he appeareth? for he is like a refiner's fire."
kjv_text: But who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth? for he is like a refiner's fire, and like fullers' sope:

saying: A voice crying in the wilderness
meaning: A lone person whose warning or idea nobody listens to.
explanation: Isaiah's prophecy, fulfilled in John the Baptist, who prepared the way for Jesus by calling people to repent.
kjv_text: For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.

meaning: A group of treacherous people.
explanation: John the Baptist to the Pharisees and Sadducees: "O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?"
kjv_text: But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?

meaning: A tough first experience of something.
explanation: John the Baptist said Jesus would baptise "with the Holy Ghost, and with fire." The modern sense of a soldier's first battle comes from the French baptême du feu.
kjv_text: I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire:

saying: Separate the wheat from the chaff
meaning: Sort out what is valuable from what is worthless.
explanation: John the Baptist said the coming Messiah would "gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire."
