kjv_text: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.

saying: Man shall not live by bread alone
variants: Man does not live by bread alone
meaning: People need more than physical things, such as meaning, beauty and faith, to truly live.
explanation: Moses told Israel that God fed them manna to teach them to depend on His word. Jesus quoted this line to resist Satan's temptation to turn stones into bread.
kjv_text: But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.

meaning: People who draw others to faith.
explanation: Jesus called the fishermen Peter and Andrew: "Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men."
kjv_text: And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.

saying: The meek shall inherit the earth
meaning: Gentle, humble people will win in the end.
explanation: From the Beatitudes, echoing Psalm 37:11. The meek are not weak. They trust God rather than grabbing for themselves.
kjv_text: Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.

meaning: Those who make peace are to be admired.
explanation: From the Beatitudes: "for they shall be called the children of God."
kjv_text: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.

meaning: A good, honest, dependable person.
explanation: Jesus told His disciples, "Ye are the salt of the earth." Salt preserves and flavours, just as they were to do good in the world.
kjv_text: Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.

meaning: A community meant to be a visible example to others.
explanation: "Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid."
kjv_text: Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.

meaning: Someone who brings hope or goodness to others.
explanation: Jesus to His disciples: "Ye are the light of the world." Of Himself: "I am the light of the world."
kjv_text: Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.

saying: Hide your light under a bushel
meaning: Be modest about, or conceal, your talents.
explanation: "Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel" (a grain basket). "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father" (5:16).
kjv_text: Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house.

meaning: Not the smallest detail.
explanation: A jot is the smallest Hebrew letter and a tittle is a tiny stroke. Jesus said none would pass from the law "till all be fulfilled."
kjv_text: For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.

meaning: Refuse to retaliate when wronged.
explanation: "Whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also." Jesus replaces "eye for eye" with non-retaliation.
kjv_text: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.

meaning: Do more than is required.
explanation: Roman soldiers could force a civilian to carry their gear for one mile. Jesus said, "go with him twain": go two.
kjv_text: And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain.

meaning: Show goodwill even to those who wrong you.
explanation: "Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you."
kjv_text: But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;

saying: Rain on the just and on the unjust
meaning: Good and bad things happen to everyone alike.
explanation: God "maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good", and Jesus called His followers to be just as generous.
kjv_text: That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.

saying: Let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth
variants: The left hand doesn't know what the right hand is doing
meaning: Originally, give in secret; today it usually means an organisation's parts are badly coordinated.
explanation: Jesus taught that giving should be done quietly, not for show, "and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly."
kjv_text: But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:

meaning: In prayer, the hope for God's rule on earth; "till kingdom come" means for ever.
explanation: From the Lord's Prayer: "Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven."
kjv_text: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.

variants: Give us this day our daily bread
meaning: The basic things needed each day, especially food or income.
explanation: From the Lord's Prayer: a request to depend on God day by day.
kjv_text: Give us this day our daily bread.

meaning: A prayer for protection.
explanation: From the Lord's Prayer: "lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil."
kjv_text: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.

meaning: Supreme might and honour.
explanation: The Lord's Prayer ends, "For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen." Graham Greene used it as a novel title.
kjv_text: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.

meaning: Invest in what lasts beyond this life.
explanation: "...where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal."
kjv_text: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:

saying: Where your treasure is, there will your heart be
meaning: What you value most reveals and shapes your heart.
explanation: Jesus' conclusion to His teaching on storing up treasure in heaven rather than on earth.
kjv_text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

saying: No man can serve two masters
meaning: You can't be fully loyal to two opposing things.
explanation: "...Ye cannot serve God and mammon" (wealth).
kjv_text: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

saying: Consider the lilies of the field
meaning: Stop worrying: God provides.
explanation: "...how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin: And yet... even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these."
kjv_text: And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:

variants: Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof
meaning: Deal with today's problems and don't worry about tomorrow's.
explanation: The close of Jesus' teaching on anxiety: "Take therefore no thought for the morrow... Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof."
kjv_text: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

saying: Judge not, lest ye be judged
meaning: Don't condemn others, or you'll be held to the same standard.
explanation: "Judge not, that ye be not judged." It is a warning against hypocritical, harsh judgment, followed by the image of the mote and the beam.
kjv_text: Judge not, that ye be not judged.

meaning: You'll be treated the way you treat others.
explanation: "...it shall be measured to you again." "Mete" means to measure out.
kjv_text: For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again.

variants: Take the plank out of your own eye
meaning: Criticising small faults in others while ignoring bigger ones in yourself.
explanation: Jesus pictures a man with a beam (a log) in his own eye trying to remove a mote (a speck of dust) from his brother's. "Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam."
kjv_text: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

meaning: Offer something valuable to people who can't appreciate it.
explanation: "Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet."
kjv_text: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.

meaning: Persistent effort will be rewarded.
explanation: "Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you." It is a promise about persistent prayer.
kjv_text: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:

variants: Do unto others as you would have them do unto you
meaning: Treat people the way you would want to be treated.
explanation: "All things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets."
kjv_text: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.

meaning: An honest, morally upright way of life.
explanation: "Strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it." "Strait" means tight or confined. "Straight" is a later spelling mix-up.
kjv_text: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.

meaning: A dangerous person who looks harmless.
explanation: "Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves."
kjv_text: Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.

meaning: Good things can't come from a bad source.
explanation: "Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?" Jesus' test for false prophets.
kjv_text: Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?

saying: By their fruits ye shall know them
variants: Judge a tree by its fruit
meaning: People are shown for who they are by what they do.
explanation: Jesus' test for false prophets. A good tree bears good fruit, and a corrupt tree bears evil fruit.
kjv_text: Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.

meaning: Having no solid foundation; bound to fail.
explanation: The foolish man built his house on sand and it fell in the storm. The wise man, who heard Jesus' words and did them, built on the rock.
kjv_text: And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand:

meaning: Great distress and anger; often used jokingly about complaints.
explanation: Jesus' description of the fate of those shut out of the kingdom: "cast out into outer darkness."
kjv_text: But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

saying: Let the dead bury their dead
meaning: Leave the past behind and focus on what matters now.
explanation: Jesus' reply to a man who wanted to bury his father before following Him. Following Christ comes first.
kjv_text: But Jesus said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.

meaning: A gentle rebuke to someone who doubts.
explanation: Jesus to His frightened disciples during a storm on the lake, just before He calmed the wind and the sea.
kjv_text: And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.

meaning: Forcing something new into an old structure that can't hold it.
explanation: Old leather wineskins burst when new, fermenting wine is poured in. Jesus' new message wouldn't fit inside old religious forms.
kjv_text: Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runneth out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.

meaning: Lost, leaderless and confused.
explanation: Jesus saw the crowds and "was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd."
kjv_text: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.

saying: Shake the dust off your feet
meaning: Leave a place with no intention of returning.
explanation: Jesus told the Twelve to do this when leaving a town that would not receive them. It was a sign that the town had rejected the message.
kjv_text: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.

saying: Wise as serpents, harmless as doves
meaning: Be shrewd but innocent.
explanation: "Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves."
kjv_text: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.

saying: The very hairs of your head are numbered
meaning: God knows and cares about every detail of your life.
explanation: Jesus told His disciples not to fear. If God cares for sparrows, how much more will He care for them.
kjv_text: But the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

saying: A reed shaken by the wind
meaning: Someone weak and easily swayed.
explanation: Jesus about John the Baptist: "What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?" John was anything but.
kjv_text: And as they departed, Jesus began to say unto the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?

saying: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear
meaning: Pay attention: this is important.
explanation: A phrase Jesus often used after a teaching or parable, calling for careful listening that leads to obedience.
kjv_text: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

meaning: A public show of sorrow or repentance.
explanation: People in mourning or repenting wore rough goat-hair cloth and sat in ashes. Jesus said Tyre and Sidon would have repented this way had they seen His miracles.
kjv_text: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

saying: He that is not with me is against me
variants: If you're not with me, you're against me
meaning: There's no neutral ground.
explanation: Jesus to those accusing Him of casting out demons by Satan: "he that gathereth not with me scattereth abroad."
kjv_text: He that is not with me is against me; and he that gathereth not with me scattereth abroad.

meaning: Fail to continue; be dropped or forgotten.
explanation: In the parable of the sower, seed that fell by the wayside was eaten by birds, a picture of hearing the word without understanding it.
kjv_text: And when he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side, and the fowls came and devoured them up:

variants: Separate the wheat from the tares
meaning: Good and bad mixed together until they can be sorted.
explanation: An enemy sowed weeds (tares) among a farmer's wheat. The master let both grow until harvest, then separated them.
kjv_text: Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn.

meaning: Something so valuable it's worth giving up everything for.
explanation: A merchant sold all he had to buy one pearl. It is a parable of the worth of the kingdom of heaven.
kjv_text: Who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.

saying: A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country
variants: A prophet is without honour in his own country
meaning: People are rarely appreciated by those who know them best.
explanation: Jesus' hometown of Nazareth took offence at Him. They knew Him as the carpenter's son.
kjv_text: And they were offended in him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house.

variants: Want someone's head on a platter
meaning: Demand harsh punishment for someone.
explanation: Herodias's daughter, prompted by her mother, asked Herod for "John Baptist's head in a charger" (a large platter).
kjv_text: And she, being before instructed of her mother, said, Give me here John Baptist's head in a charger.

meaning: A small supply that miraculously stretches to meet a large need.
explanation: Jesus fed five thousand men, plus women and children, from five loaves and two fish, with twelve baskets left over.
kjv_text: And they say unto him, We have here but five loaves, and two fishes.

variants: Thinks he can walk on water
meaning: Seem able to do the impossible; often said of someone treated as flawless.
explanation: Jesus walked on the Sea of Galilee to His disciples' boat, and Peter briefly walked to meet Him until he looked at the waves.
kjv_text: And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea.

meaning: Uninformed people guiding others who know no better.
explanation: Jesus on the Pharisees: "if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch."
kjv_text: Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch.

variants: Crumbs from the rich man's table
meaning: Small leftovers after others have taken the best.
explanation: A Canaanite woman answered Jesus with humble persistence: even the dogs eat the crumbs. Jesus praised her great faith.
kjv_text: And she said, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table.

variants: Red sky at night, shepherd's delight
meaning: Weather lore: a red evening sky means fair weather tomorrow.
explanation: Jesus: "When it is evening, ye say, It will be fair weather: for the sky is red." He was rebuking people who could read the weather but not the signs of the times.
kjv_text: He answered and said unto them, When it is evening, ye say, It will be fair weather: for the sky is red.

meaning: Something typical of the present age.
explanation: "O ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky; but can ye not discern the signs of the times?"
kjv_text: And in the morning, It will be foul weather to day: for the sky is red and lowring. O ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky; but can ye not discern the signs of the times?

meaning: Human nature; one's own family.
explanation: Jesus to Peter: "flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven." Here it means merely human understanding.
kjv_text: And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.

meaning: Authority or the means of access to something.
explanation: Jesus to Peter after his confession: "I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven."
kjv_text: And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.

meaning: A firm rejection of temptation.
explanation: Jesus rebuking Peter for trying to talk Him out of the cross: "thou savourest not the things that be of God."
kjv_text: But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.

meaning: Belief can achieve what seems impossible.
explanation: "If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove."
kjv_text: And Jesus said unto them, Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you.

meaning: A heavy burden that holds you back.
explanation: Jesus' warning: whoever causes a little one to stumble would be better off drowned with a millstone hung round his neck.
kjv_text: But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.

meaning: Forgive endlessly.
explanation: Peter asked if forgiving seven times was enough. Jesus answered, "Until seventy times seven", meaning without keeping count.
kjv_text: Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.

saying: What God hath joined together, let not man put asunder
meaning: Marriage should not be broken apart.
explanation: Jesus' teaching on marriage, quoting Genesis 2:24. It is used in wedding vows to this day.
kjv_text: Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

saying: Through the eye of a needle
variants: A camel through the eye of a needle
meaning: Something nearly impossible.
explanation: "It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God." With God, Jesus added, all things are possible.
kjv_text: And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.

meaning: At the last possible moment.
explanation: In the parable, workers hired "about the eleventh hour" (late afternoon, one hour before quitting) got a full day's pay.
kjv_text: And when they came that were hired about the eleventh hour, they received every man a penny.

saying: Bear the burden and heat of the day
meaning: Do the hardest part of the work.
explanation: In the parable of the labourers, the all-day workers complained that the last-hired got equal pay though "we have borne the burden and heat of the day."
kjv_text: Saying, These last have wrought but one hour, and thou hast made them equal unto us, which have borne the burden and heat of the day.

meaning: Those who seem least important now will be honoured most.
explanation: The close of the parable of the labourers in the vineyard. God's generosity overturns human rankings.
kjv_text: So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.

meaning: A place full of crooked dealing.
explanation: Jesus drove the money-changers from the temple: "My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves."
kjv_text: And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.

saying: Many are called, but few are chosen
meaning: Many are invited or try, but few succeed.
explanation: The end of the parable of the wedding feast, where invited guests refuse to come and one guest arrives without a wedding garment.
kjv_text: For many are called, but few are chosen.

variants: Render unto Caesar the things that are Caesar's
meaning: Give the state (or anyone) what is rightly theirs.
explanation: Asked if Jews should pay taxes to Rome, Jesus showed a coin with Caesar's image: "Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and unto God the things that are God's."
kjv_text: They say unto him, Caesar's. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and unto God the things that are God's.

saying: Strain at a gnat and swallow a camel
meaning: Fuss over trivia while ignoring what matters.
explanation: Jesus to the Pharisees, who tithed their herbs but neglected "judgment, mercy, and faith."
kjv_text: Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.

meaning: Hypocrites who look good outside but are corrupt inside.
explanation: Jesus' rebuke to the scribes and Pharisees: tombs "beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones."
kjv_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness.

meaning: A time of conflict and constant alarm.
explanation: Jesus warned His disciples of this before the end: "see that ye be not troubled... but the end is not yet."
kjv_text: And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.

variants: Well done, good and faithful servant
meaning: Praise for loyal, diligent work.
explanation: The master's words to the servants who put their talents to work in the parable of the talents.
kjv_text: His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.

saying: Hide your talent in the earth
meaning: Waste your gifts by not using them.
explanation: In the parable, a talent was a large sum of money. The servant who buried his out of fear was condemned. The English word "talent" meaning a natural gift comes from this parable.
kjv_text: And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth: lo, there thou hast that is thine.

saying: Separate the sheep from the goats
meaning: Sort out the good from the bad.
explanation: At the final judgment, the Son of Man divides the nations "as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats", by how they treated "the least of these."
kjv_text: And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats:

meaning: The price of betrayal.
explanation: What the chief priests paid Judas to betray Jesus. It fulfilled Zechariah 11:12-13.
kjv_text: And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.

saying: Let this cup pass from me
meaning: A plea to be spared an ordeal.
explanation: Jesus' prayer in Gethsemane: "O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt."
kjv_text: And he went a little farther, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.

saying: The spirit is willing but the flesh is weak
meaning: You mean well but lack the strength to follow through.
explanation: Jesus in Gethsemane found His disciples asleep when He had asked them to watch and pray.
kjv_text: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.

meaning: An act of betrayal disguised as friendship.
explanation: Judas signalled which man to arrest by greeting Jesus with a kiss.
kjv_text: And forthwith he came to Jesus, and said, Hail, master; and kissed him.

saying: Live by the sword, die by the sword
meaning: Violence brings violence on those who use it.
explanation: Jesus to Peter, who drew his sword at the arrest: "all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword."
kjv_text: Then said Jesus unto him, Put up again thy sword into his place: for all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword.

meaning: Money gained at the cost of someone's life.
explanation: When Judas threw the thirty pieces back, the priests wouldn't put them in the treasury "because it is the price of blood". They bought a potter's field with it instead.
kjv_text: And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood.

meaning: A burial ground for the poor or unknown.
explanation: The chief priests used Judas's thirty pieces of silver to buy the potter's field "to bury strangers in."
kjv_text: And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter's field, to bury strangers in.

meaning: Refuse any further responsibility.
explanation: Pilate washed his hands before the crowd, claiming he was innocent of Jesus' blood, even as he handed Him over to be crucified.
kjv_text: When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but that rather a tumult was made, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it.

meaning: A position of honour that brings suffering.
explanation: The soldiers mocked Jesus by pressing a crown of thorns onto His head.
kjv_text: And when they had platted a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand: and they bowed the knee before him, and mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews!

saying: The sabbath was made for man
meaning: Rules exist to serve people, not the other way round.
explanation: "...and not man for the sabbath." Jesus answered the Pharisees who objected to His disciples plucking grain on the sabbath.
kjv_text: And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:

saying: A house divided against itself cannot stand
meaning: A group split by internal conflict will fail.
explanation: Jesus answering the charge that He cast out demons by Satan's power. Abraham Lincoln famously quoted it in 1858.
kjv_text: And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand.

meaning: Be ignored or have no effect.
explanation: In the parable of the sower, seed that falls on stony ground springs up quickly but withers because it has no root.
kjv_text: And some fell on stony ground, where it had not much earth; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of earth:

meaning: A headlong stampede toward disaster.
explanation: Jesus cast demons out of a man into a herd of about two thousand pigs, which "ran violently down a steep place into the sea."
kjv_text: And forthwith Jesus gave them leave. And the unclean spirits went out, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea, (they were about two thousand;) and were choked in the sea.

variants: All things are possible to him that believeth
meaning: Nothing is impossible with faith.
explanation: Jesus to the father of a boy with an evil spirit. The father replied, "Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief."
kjv_text: Jesus said unto him, If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth.

meaning: Let children come; welcome them.
explanation: Jesus, displeased that His disciples were turning children away: "forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God." "Suffer" means allow.
kjv_text: But when Jesus saw it, he was much displeased, and said unto them, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.

meaning: A small gift that means much because it costs the giver so much.
explanation: A poor widow gave two mites, the smallest coins. Jesus said she gave more than all the rich, "for she of her want did cast in all that she had."
kjv_text: And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites, which make a farthing.

meaning: No space or welcome available.
explanation: Mary laid the newborn Jesus in a manger "because there was no room for them in the inn."
kjv_text: And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.

saying: Peace on earth, goodwill toward men
meaning: A Christmas greeting wishing peace for all.
explanation: The angels' song to the shepherds at Jesus' birth: "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men."
kjv_text: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.

meaning: Fix your own faults before criticising others.
explanation: Jesus anticipated the Nazareth crowd quoting this proverb at Him, demanding miracles at home like the ones done in Capernaum.
kjv_text: And he said unto them, Ye will surely say unto me this proverb, Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country.

meaning: As an extra, beyond what's needed.
explanation: "Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over." A generous grain merchant filled the measure to overflowing.
kjv_text: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.

saying: Nothing is secret that shall not be made known
meaning: The truth always comes out eventually.
explanation: "For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad."
kjv_text: For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.

saying: Put your hand to the plough
variants: No turning back from the plough
meaning: Commit fully to a task without looking back.
explanation: "No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God."
kjv_text: And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.

saying: The labourer is worthy of his hire
meaning: Workers deserve fair pay.
explanation: Jesus to the seventy He sent out: accept the hospitality offered, because the worker deserves his wages.
kjv_text: And in the same house remain, eating and drinking such things as they give: for the labourer is worthy of his hire. Go not from house to house.

saying: Pass by on the other side
meaning: Ignore someone in need.
explanation: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, a priest and then a Levite saw the wounded man and "passed by on the other side."
kjv_text: And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.

meaning: A stranger who helps someone in need.
explanation: In Jesus' parable, a priest and a Levite passed by a beaten man, but a Samaritan, a despised outsider, stopped and cared for him. "Go, and do thou likewise."
kjv_text: But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him,

meaning: Announce something publicly and loudly.
explanation: "That which ye have spoken in the ear in closets shall be proclaimed upon the housetops." Flat rooftops were public places in Israel.
kjv_text: Therefore whatsoever ye have spoken in darkness shall be heard in the light; and that which ye have spoken in the ear in closets shall be proclaimed upon the housetops.

meaning: A burden or trial you must carry.
explanation: "Whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple." In the Gospels it is about following Christ whatever it costs.
kjv_text: And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.

meaning: Weigh the price before committing.
explanation: Jesus compared following Him to building a tower: "sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?"
kjv_text: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?

meaning: Someone who has strayed and is sought until found.
explanation: A shepherd leaves ninety-nine sheep to find the one lost one. "Joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth."
kjv_text: What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?

meaning: Someone who leaves, wastes everything, and comes home repentant.
explanation: A younger son squandered his inheritance "with riotous living". When he came home, his father ran to welcome him. It is a picture of God's grace.
kjv_text: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.

meaning: Throw a lavish celebration, especially for a homecoming.
explanation: The father's order when his prodigal son returned: "bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry."
kjv_text: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:

meaning: Unharmed.
explanation: The servant told the prodigal's older brother: "thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound."
kjv_text: And he said unto him, Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.

meaning: A divide that can't be crossed.
explanation: Abraham to the rich man in torment: "between us and you there is a great gulf fixed."
kjv_text: And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.

meaning: A self-righteous hypocrite.
explanation: In Jesus' parable, a Pharisee prayed, "God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are." But it was the humble tax collector who went home justified.
kjv_text: The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican.

meaning: A very short distance.
explanation: In Gethsemane, Jesus "was withdrawn from them about a stone's cast, and kneeled down, and prayed."
kjv_text: And he was withdrawn from them about a stone's cast, and kneeled down, and prayed,

meaning: Work extremely hard or suffer intense anxiety.
explanation: In Gethsemane, Jesus prayed in such agony that "his sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground."
kjv_text: And being in an agony he prayed more earnestly: and his sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground.

saying: Forgive them, for they know not what they do
meaning: A plea to excuse people who act in ignorance.
explanation: Jesus' prayer from the cross for those crucifying Him.
kjv_text: Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots.

saying: In the beginning was the Word
meaning: Language or reason comes first; a reference to the origin of all things.
explanation: John opens his Gospel by echoing Genesis 1:1: "and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." The Word is Christ, who "was made flesh" (1:14).
kjv_text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

meaning: Transform something ordinary into something special; do the impossible.
explanation: Jesus' first miracle, at a wedding in Cana of Galilee, where the wine had run out.
kjv_text: When the ruler of the feast had tasted the water that was made wine, and knew not whence it was: (but the servants which drew the water knew;) the governor of the feast called the bridegroom,

variants: Keep the best wine until last
meaning: Hold back the finest thing until the end.
explanation: At the wedding in Cana, after Jesus turned water into wine, the governor of the feast told the bridegroom, "thou hast kept the good wine until now."
kjv_text: And saith unto him, Every man at the beginning doth set forth good wine; and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse: but thou hast kept the good wine until now.

meaning: Spiritually renewed; more loosely, having found new enthusiasm.
explanation: Jesus to Nicodemus: "Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God."
kjv_text: Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.

saying: The wind bloweth where it listeth
meaning: Some things move by forces beyond our control or understanding.
explanation: Jesus to Nicodemus about the Spirit: "thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth."
kjv_text: The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.

meaning: Something essential for survival.
explanation: "I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger." It is one of Jesus' "I am" sayings.
kjv_text: And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.

meaning: Be the first to criticise, though you're not blameless yourself.
explanation: Scribes brought a woman caught in adultery to Jesus. He said, "He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her." One by one they left.
kjv_text: So when they continued asking him, he lifted up himself, and said unto them, He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.

saying: The truth shall make you free
variants: The truth will set you free
meaning: Knowing the truth brings freedom.
explanation: "Ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free." In context the truth is Jesus' word, and the freedom is from sin (8:34-36).
kjv_text: And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

meaning: The devil; a chronic deceiver.
explanation: Jesus said of the devil: "When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it."
kjv_text: Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.

meaning: A caring, self-sacrificing leader.
explanation: "I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep."
kjv_text: I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.

meaning: An exclamation of exasperation or dismay; the shortest verse in the KJV.
explanation: At the tomb of his friend Lazarus, moments before raising him from the dead, Jesus wept, showing His compassion.
kjv_text: Jesus wept.

saying: The poor you have always with you
meaning: Poverty will never be completely gone.
explanation: Jesus defending Mary's costly anointing: "the poor always ye have with you; but me ye have not always." It echoes Deuteronomy 15:11, which commands generosity.
kjv_text: For the poor always ye have with you; but me ye have not always.

meaning: Care for each other.
explanation: Jesus' "new commandment" to His disciples: "as I have loved you, that ye also love one another."
kjv_text: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.

saying: Let not your heart be troubled
meaning: Don't worry; take comfort.
explanation: Jesus to His disciples the night before the cross: "ye believe in God, believe also in me."
kjv_text: Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me.

variants: In my Father's house are many mansions
meaning: There is room for many kinds of people.
explanation: Jesus comforting His disciples: "I go to prepare a place for you."
kjv_text: In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.

meaning: Laying down your life for others is the highest love.
explanation: "Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends." Jesus said it the night before He died.
kjv_text: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

meaning: Take heart; stay cheerful.
explanation: "In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world."
kjv_text: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.

meaning: A sceptical question about whether truth can be known.
explanation: Pilate's reply when Jesus said He came "to bear witness unto the truth." Pilate walked out without waiting for an answer.
kjv_text: Pilate saith unto him, What is truth? And when he had said this, he went out again unto the Jews, and saith unto them, I find in him no fault at all.

meaning: A sceptic who won't believe without proof.
explanation: Thomas wouldn't believe in the resurrection until he saw Jesus' wounds. When Jesus appeared, Thomas confessed, "My Lord and my God."
kjv_text: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came. The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.

meaning: Your children; now often humorous.
explanation: Peter at Pentecost: God swore to David "that of the fruit of his loins... he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
kjv_text: Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;

meaning: A sudden, life-changing change of mind.
explanation: Saul, on his way to arrest Christians in Damascus, was struck down by a light from heaven and met the risen Jesus. He became the apostle Paul.
kjv_text: And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven:

meaning: Hurt yourself by resisting what can't be changed.
explanation: A "prick" was a pointed goad for oxen. The risen Jesus used the image to Saul, who was fighting against God.
kjv_text: And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

saying: The scales fell from my eyes
meaning: Suddenly see the truth clearly.
explanation: When Ananias laid hands on the blinded Saul, "there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight."
kjv_text: And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.

meaning: Treating everyone the same, regardless of status.
explanation: Peter, at the Gentile Cornelius's house: "Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons."
kjv_text: Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons:

meaning: A great commotion.
explanation: When Peter escaped from prison with an angel's help, "there was no small stir among the soldiers, what was become of Peter."
kjv_text: Now as soon as it was day, there was no small stir among the soldiers, what was become of Peter.

meaning: Cause dramatic change.
explanation: The mob at Thessalonica complained about Paul and Silas: "These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also."
kjv_text: And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also;

saying: It is more blessed to give than to receive
variants: Better to give than to receive
meaning: Giving brings more joy than getting.
explanation: Paul quotes these words of Jesus, which are not recorded in the Gospels, to the Ephesian elders.
kjv_text: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.

meaning: Out of your mind with emotion.
explanation: Festus interrupted Paul's defence: "Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad."
kjv_text: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.

meaning: People who ignore the rules and act as they please.
explanation: Paul meant that Gentiles without Moses' law still show the law written on their hearts. The modern meaning has shifted to rule-ignoring.
kjv_text: For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves:

saying: The wages of sin is death
meaning: Wrongdoing brings its own punishment.
explanation: "For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord."
kjv_text: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

saying: All things work together for good
meaning: Even bad circumstances can lead to good in the end.
explanation: "...to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose."
kjv_text: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.

variants: Vengeance is mine, saith the Lord
meaning: Leave revenge to God.
explanation: "Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves... for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord."
kjv_text: Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.

saying: Heap coals of fire on his head
variants: Heap burning coals on someone's head
meaning: Shame an enemy by treating them kindly.
explanation: "If thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink." Kindness may bring an enemy to burning remorse and repentance.
kjv_text: Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head.

meaning: Answer wrong with kindness.
explanation: "Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good."
kjv_text: Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.

meaning: The people in authority.
explanation: "The powers that be are ordained of God." Paul was teaching Christians to respect civil authority.
kjv_text: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.

meaning: Past the moment when something should happen.
explanation: "Now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed."
kjv_text: And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.

meaning: An obstacle to progress.
explanation: Paul urges believers not to put "a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall" in a brother's way, by using their freedom carelessly.
kjv_text: Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in his brother's way.

meaning: Paid for at great cost.
explanation: "For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body."
kjv_text: For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's.

meaning: Knowledge alone can make a person arrogant.
explanation: "Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth." Paul was answering believers who were proud of their knowledge about food offered to idols.
kjv_text: Now as touching things offered unto idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth.

meaning: Trying to please everyone.
explanation: Paul adapted to every culture "that I might by all means save some." Today the phrase is often critical, but Paul meant it as loving flexibility.
kjv_text: To the weak became I as weak, that I might gain the weak: I am made all things to all men, that I might by all means save some.

saying: Sounding brass and a tinkling cymbal
meaning: Impressive words that are empty without love.
explanation: "Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal."
kjv_text: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.

meaning: Seeing or understanding only dimly.
explanation: "For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face." Ancient mirrors ("glass") gave only a blurred reflection.
kjv_text: For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.

meaning: The three great virtues.
explanation: "And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity." "Charity" here is love.
kjv_text: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.

meaning: Properly and in an organised way.
explanation: Paul's closing instruction on orderly worship: "Let all things be done decently and in order."
kjv_text: Let all things be done decently and in order.

meaning: Death, the final thing to be conquered.
explanation: Paul on the resurrection: Christ will reign until He has put all enemies under His feet, and death is the last.
kjv_text: The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death.

meaning: Everything considered; or everything to someone.
explanation: At the end, the Son hands the kingdom to the Father, "that God may be all in all."
kjv_text: And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all.

saying: In the twinkling of an eye
meaning: In an instant.
explanation: At the resurrection, "we shall all be changed, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump."
kjv_text: In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.

saying: O death, where is thy sting?
meaning: Death has lost its power to frighten.
explanation: Paul's triumphant cry about the resurrection: "O grave, where is thy victory?"
kjv_text: O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?

meaning: Strict, literal rules rather than their intended purpose.
explanation: "The letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life." Paul contrasts the written code with the Spirit's new covenant.
kjv_text: Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life.

meaning: Something precious held in something fragile.
explanation: Paul describes the gospel in weak human messengers, "that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us."
kjv_text: But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us.

saying: Walk by faith, not by sight
meaning: Trust even what you can't see.
explanation: Paul on living in hope of the unseen, eternal home with the Lord.
kjv_text: (For we walk by faith, not by sight:)

meaning: Poorly matched as partners, especially in marriage.
explanation: "Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers." Two animals of different strength can't pull a yoke together.
kjv_text: Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?

meaning: Give gladly, not grudgingly.
explanation: "Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity."
kjv_text: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.

meaning: Be patient with foolish people; usually used in the negative.
explanation: Paul, with irony, to the Corinthians: "For ye suffer fools gladly, seeing ye yourselves are wise."
kjv_text: For ye suffer fools gladly, seeing ye yourselves are wise.

meaning: A persistent annoyance or problem.
explanation: Paul's unnamed affliction "lest I should be exalted above measure." God answered, "My grace is sufficient for thee."
kjv_text: And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure.

meaning: A welcome into partnership.
explanation: James, Peter and John gave Paul and Barnabas "the right hands of fellowship" and agreed to their mission to the Gentiles.
kjv_text: And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.

meaning: At exactly the right moment.
explanation: "But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman."
kjv_text: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,

meaning: Lose your good reputation or position.
explanation: Paul warns those who try to be justified by the law: "ye are fallen from grace." It means turning from grace to rely on law.
kjv_text: Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.

saying: A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump
meaning: A small bad influence can spread and corrupt everything.
explanation: Paul warns that a small amount of false teaching, like yeast in dough, soon affects the whole church.
kjv_text: A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.

meaning: Help each other through difficulties.
explanation: "...and so fulfil the law of Christ."
kjv_text: Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.

variants: As you sow, so shall you reap
meaning: Your actions have consequences to match.
explanation: "Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap."
kjv_text: Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.

meaning: For ever.
explanation: "Unto him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end. Amen."
kjv_text: Unto him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end. Amen.

saying: Let not the sun go down upon your wrath
variants: Don't let the sun go down on your anger
meaning: Settle quarrels before the day ends.
explanation: "Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath."
kjv_text: Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath:

meaning: Make the most of every opportunity.
explanation: "Redeeming the time, because the days are evil."
kjv_text: Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.

saying: Put on the whole armour of God
meaning: Prepare yourself spiritually for struggle.
explanation: Paul pictures the Christian as a soldier with truth, righteousness, faith and salvation, and the Spirit's sword.
kjv_text: Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.

meaning: Unseen spiritual forces; the powers that rule.
explanation: "For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world."
kjv_text: For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.

meaning: Find your own way through a problem.
explanation: "...with fear and trembling. For it is God which worketh in you." Paul means living out the salvation God has already given.
kjv_text: Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.

meaning: Keep striving toward your goal.
explanation: "I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus." Paul pictures a runner straining for the finish.
kjv_text: I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.

saying: The peace that passeth all understanding
meaning: A calm that doesn't make sense given the circumstances.
explanation: "And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus."
kjv_text: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.

meaning: Work done for love rather than pay.
explanation: Paul remembers the Thessalonians' "work of faith, and labour of love, and patience of hope."
kjv_text: Remembering without ceasing your work of faith, and labour of love, and patience of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, in the sight of God and our Father;

saying: Like a thief in the night
meaning: Suddenly and without warning.
explanation: "The day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night." It is a call to stay awake and ready.
kjv_text: For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night.

meaning: People who meddle in others' business.
explanation: Paul on some in Thessalonica "working not at all, but are busybodies." He told them to work quietly and earn their own bread.
kjv_text: For we hear that there are some which walk among you disorderly, working not at all, but are busybodies.

saying: Be not weary in well doing
variants: Don't grow weary in doing good
meaning: Keep doing good even when it's tiring.
explanation: Galatians adds: "for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not."
kjv_text: But ye, brethren, be not weary in well doing.

meaning: Money, especially money gained dishonestly; now often humorous.
explanation: A church leader must be "not greedy of filthy lucre", that is, of shameful gain.
kjv_text: Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous;

meaning: Deceitful; saying different things to different people.
explanation: Deacons must be "grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine."
kjv_text: Likewise must the deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre;

meaning: Traditional beliefs that aren't true.
explanation: "Refuse profane and old wives' fables, and exercise thyself rather unto godliness."
kjv_text: But refuse profane and old wives' fables, and exercise thyself rather unto godliness.

saying: You can't take it with you
meaning: Possessions are of no use after death.
explanation: "For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out." See also Job 1:21.
kjv_text: For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.

saying: The love of money is the root of all evil
variants: Money is the root of all evil
meaning: Greed leads to every kind of wrongdoing.
explanation: Often misquoted as "money is the root of all evil." Paul blames the love of money, not money itself.
kjv_text: For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.

meaning: Keep striving for what is right.
explanation: "Fight the good fight of faith." At the end of his life Paul wrote, "I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course."
kjv_text: Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.

meaning: The living and the dead; everyone.
explanation: "Quick" meant alive. Christ "shall judge the quick and the dead". The phrase is repeated in the Apostles' Creed.
kjv_text: I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom;

meaning: Wanting to hear only what pleases you.
explanation: Paul warned that people would gather teachers "having itching ears", who tell them what they want to hear.
kjv_text: For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;

saying: Out of the mouth of the lion
meaning: Rescued from great danger.
explanation: Paul, deserted at his trial: "the Lord stood with me... and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion."
kjv_text: Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.

saying: To the pure all things are pure
meaning: A clean heart sees innocence where others see wrong.
explanation: "...but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure."
kjv_text: Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled.

meaning: Something with both good and bad effects.
explanation: "The word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword." It cuts deep and exposes the heart.
kjv_text: For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.

meaning: A place or state of hoped-for happiness.
explanation: Canaan, the land God promised to Abraham's descendants. Hebrews says Abraham "sojourned in the land of promise" by faith, looking for a heavenly city.
kjv_text: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:

meaning: People who don't belong to this world.
explanation: The heroes of faith "confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth", seeking a heavenly country.
kjv_text: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.

meaning: A great crowd of people who have gone before, as examples.
explanation: After listing the heroes of faith, Hebrews urges believers to "run with patience the race that is set before us."
kjv_text: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,

meaning: Showing kindness to strangers who may be more than they seem.
explanation: "Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares", as Abraham did (Genesis 18).
kjv_text: Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.

saying: Swift to hear, slow to speak
variants: Quick to listen, slow to speak
meaning: Listen more than you talk, and don't get angry quickly.
explanation: "Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath."
kjv_text: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:

meaning: Control what you say.
explanation: "If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue... this man's religion is vain."
kjv_text: If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man's religion is vain.

meaning: Beliefs mean nothing unless you act on them.
explanation: "For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also."
kjv_text: For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

meaning: If nothing prevents it.
explanation: James warned against boasting about tomorrow's plans: "Ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that."
kjv_text: For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.

meaning: Great endurance under long trials.
explanation: James points to Job as an example: "Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy."
kjv_text: Behold, we count them happy which endure. Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy.

meaning: Mean what you say; no need for oaths.
explanation: "Swear not... but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay."
kjv_text: But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.

meaning: Old-fashioned way of referring to women.
explanation: Husbands are to honour their wives "as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life."
kjv_text: Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.

meaning: Hide many faults; now often joking ("a coat of paint covers a multitude of sins").
explanation: "Charity shall cover the multitude of sins." Love forgives and overlooks offences.
kjv_text: And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins.

meaning: Stuck in a bad state, especially of one's own making.
explanation: "The sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire." Peter uses the proverb for those who go back to sin.
kjv_text: But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.

meaning: Love is God's very nature.
explanation: "He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love."
kjv_text: He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.

meaning: The beginning and the end; the whole of something.
explanation: Alpha and omega are the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet. God declares, "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending."
kjv_text: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty.

meaning: Loyal to the very end.
explanation: Jesus to the church at Smyrna, facing persecution: "and I will give thee a crown of life."
kjv_text: Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.

saying: Rule with a rod of iron
meaning: Govern harshly and strictly.
explanation: The Messiah's victory over the rebellious nations is pictured as breaking them "with a rod of iron". Revelation promises the same authority to those who overcome.
kjv_text: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father.

meaning: Half-hearted and uncommitted.
explanation: Jesus to the church at Laodicea: "because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth."
kjv_text: So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth.

saying: The four horsemen of the Apocalypse
meaning: Harbingers of disaster: conquest, war, famine and death.
explanation: As the Lamb opens the first four seals, riders on white, red, black and pale horses bring judgment on the earth.
kjv_text: And I looked, and behold a pale horse: and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him. And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth.

meaning: Hell, or something that endlessly consumes ("a bottomless pit of debt").
explanation: In Revelation, the abyss from which destructive forces are released and where Satan is later bound.
kjv_text: And the fifth angel sounded, and I saw a star fall from heaven unto the earth: and to him was given the key of the bottomless pit.

meaning: An unpleasant surprise at the end.
explanation: In John's vision, the locusts from the bottomless pit have "tails like unto scorpions, and there were stings in their tails."
kjv_text: And they had tails like unto scorpions, and there were stings in their tails: and their power was to hurt men five months.

meaning: Built-up anger ready to burst out; God's judgment.
explanation: An angel gathers the vine of the earth into "the great winepress of the wrath of God." The "Battle Hymn of the Republic" and Steinbeck's novel made the phrase famous.
kjv_text: And the angel thrust in his sickle into the earth, and gathered the vine of the earth, and cast it into the great winepress of the wrath of God.

meaning: A sign of allegiance to evil; used for anything feared as sinister control.
explanation: In Revelation, the beast forces everyone to take its mark on the right hand or forehead in order to buy or sell.
kjv_text: And the first went, and poured out his vial upon the earth; and there fell a noisome and grievous sore upon the men which had the mark of the beast, and upon them which worshipped his image.

meaning: A final, catastrophic conflict.
explanation: The place where the kings of the earth gather for battle on "that great day of God Almighty."
kjv_text: And he gathered them together into a place called in the Hebrew tongue Armageddon.

meaning: God's record of those who belong to Him.
explanation: At the final judgment "another book was opened, which is the book of life."
kjv_text: And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.

meaning: An ideal, perfect city or society.
explanation: John saw "the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride."
kjv_text: And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.

meaning: Solid, firm and unwavering.
explanation: "And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth." The New Jerusalem is a perfect cube.
kjv_text: And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.

meaning: A place of easy wealth.
explanation: In the New Jerusalem, "the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass."
kjv_text: And the twelve gates were twelve pearls; every several gate was of one pearl: and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass.
